samples.summary: Gate 1b's fail-closed comment now misdescribes gate 1's error handling, which this delta just changed
samples.evidence: `ranBaseCiDefinition`'s catch block documents its choice as "Exit 1 (a gate said no) rather than 2, matching gate 1's own treatment of an unreadable Actions API" (mark-ready.mjs:276-278). After this delta, gate 1 does the opposite: an unreadable Actions API in `ciPassed` now `process.exit(2)`s (mark-ready.mjs:188). The two evidence-failure paths are both fail-closed (neither promotes), so there is no exploit here — but this is a comment that exists specifically to justify a security posture, and it now points a future maintainer at a rule that no longer exists. Someone "restoring parity" from this stale text is as likely to move gate 1b's refusal semantics as gate 1's, and gate 1b's refusal is the one that must remain a plain gate refusal (`checks.mjs` CI_DEFINING_PATHS surface / the exit-1 branch the promote job greps for a verdict line at agent-review-panel.yml:1539). The test suite pins the exit codes but nothing pins the prose.

samples.summary: New error path logs the raw execFileSync `err.message`, which carries the failed `gh` invocation and the child's stderr into a public Actions log
samples.evidence: The added `console.error` interpolates `err.message` from `execFileSync` (mark-ready.mjs:185). Node builds that message as `Command failed: <cmd>\n<stderr>`, so the promote step's log (redirected then `cat`-ed at agent-review-panel.yml:1509/1516, public for a public repo) now also carries whatever `gh` wrote to stderr for the failing request — e.g. API response bodies. I traced the credential handling and could NOT complete an exposure chain: GH_TOKEN/GH_MUTATION_TOKEN are passed via env (mark-ready.mjs:128-130), never in argv, `gh` does not echo them, and Actions masks registered secrets — so this is hardening only, not a leak I can demonstrate. Noted because the same pattern is repeated at :145, :353, :382 and :415, and one of those (:353/:382) prints the message of a call made with the App token; if `gh` ever gains a diagnostic that echoes the token it received, all five sites publish it at once. Logging `err.message` only after stripping the command echo (or logging just the HTTP status) would remove the class.

finding.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_PATHS` (checks.mjs:123-135) covers `scripts/verify-*.mjs` and `scripts/changed-areas.mjs`, but `scripts/verify-self.mjs:2-3` imports two further modules at module scope that the list does not match:

  import { extractFailureSummary } from "./failure-summary.mjs";   // scripts/failure-summary.mjs
  import { readHeadSha } from "./agent/git-env.mjs";               // scripts/agent/git-env.mjs

`definesCi("scripts/failure-summary.mjs")` and `definesCi("scripts/agent/git-env.mjs")` both return false (neither starts with `verify-`; `scripts/agent/**` is not on the list at all).

Attack: an `agent:managed` PR (or the agent App itself — both paths are explicitly named as unrestricted in mark-ready.mjs:29-32) adds a top-level side effect to `scripts/failure-summary.mjs`, e.g. `process.exit(0)` or a `process.on('exit')` override. ESM evaluates it before `verify-self.mjs`'s body runs, so `pnpm verify:self` (ci.yml:308) exits 0 having executed zero lanes and the CI run concludes `success`. Then:
  * gate 1 (`ciPassed`, mark-ready.mjs:159) reads that genuinely green run at the genuine path — passes;
  * gate 1b (`ranBaseCiDefinition`, mark-ready.mjs:224) enumerates `pulls/N/files`, finds only `scripts/failure-summary.mjs`, `definesCi` says false — passes;
  * mark-ready.mjs:382-389 then posts a hand-off comment telling the accountable human signer that "the CI definition that run executed came from `main` rather than from the branch", which is false.

Same class, also unmatched by the list: `packages/cli/vitest.config.ts` and `packages/design-sandbox/vitest.config.ts` (ci.yml:318/322 run `vitest` per package, and the config chooses which files are collected — `include: []` yields a green lane with no tests); `scripts/agent/package.json` / lockfile (the `agent:tests` lane); a newly added root `.npmrc` or `.pnpmfile.cjs` (read by `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, ci.yml:300). The comment at checks.mjs:116-121 scopes the residue to "a branch can always edit its own te

verdict.reason: Gate 1b's refusal surface is a single hard-coded list (checks.mjs:123-135) with exactly one consumer (mark-ready.mjs:205-284, via definesCi). It does not match scripts/failure-summary.mjs or scripts/agent/git-env.mjs, both of which verify-self.mjs imports at module scope (verify-self.mjs:2-3) and which therefore execute before any lane when ci.yml:308 runs `pnpm verify:self` (package.json:25). The exclusion is deliberate, not incidental: checks.test.mjs:537-548 asserts definesCi("scripts/agent/checks.mjs") === false, and the true-list at checks.test.mjs:516-532 contains no other scripts/ paths. I searched for a compensating guard and found none: the promote job (agent-review-panel.yml:1453-1550) adds no path check beyond mark-ready; harness.config.json:52-60 ciConfig is the same list minus two entries and only forces a full run (changed-areas.mjs:403); ci.yml has no post-verify:self assertion that lanes ran, the harness-report upload (ci.yml:360-367) omits if-no-files-found: error, and ci-report.yml:384 reports a missing lane report as prose under continue-on-error; CODEOWNERS:30-61 covers /scripts/agent/ and /scripts/verify-*.mjs but not scripts/failure-summary.mjs and self-documents (lines 50-52) that it binds only when branch protection enables code-owner review. So a top-level `process.exit(0)` in scripts/failure-summary.mjs yields a genuinely green CI run at the genuine workflow path with zero verify-self lanes executed, gate 1 (mark-ready.mjs:159-193) passes, gate 1b (mark-ready.mjs:236-284) sees no CI-defining hit and passes, and mark-ready.mjs:394-399 posts a hand-off comment asserting to the accountable human signer that "the CI definition that run executed came from `main`" — a false claim in the enforced output path. In-lane as a weakened/bypassable gate; major impact since human merge approval still stands but is actively misinformed.

mergedFrom.summary: The change enumerates every display-name-triggered `workflow_run` consumer and omits capture-collect.yml, which is triggered by display name and holds a cross-repo push secret

finding.summary: `capture-collect.yml` is the same forgery class the change hardens elsewhere and got no `path` clause: it consumes `workflow_run` by display name with no path / branch / head-repository guard while holding a cross-repo write PAT
finding.evidence:
This change adds `github.event.workflow_run.path == '.github/workflows/ci.yml'` to agent-review-panel.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and ci-report.yml, and checks.test.mjs's new "every workflow_run consumer" test enumerates exactly those three. capture-collect.yml consumes the same event class and is left open:

  line 67-69: `workflow_run: workflows: ["Agent Review Panel", "Agent Review On-Demand"]` — display names, which the diff's own reasoning establishes are only a `name:` key and are not unique.
  line 129: `if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_run' || github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'skipped' }}` — the only gate. No `path`, no `head_branch`, no `head_repository.full_name == github.repository`.
  line 142-146: `actions/checkout` of `dlgpdmsly2/wafflebase-agent-eval` with `token: ${{ secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN }}` (documented at line 20-23 as a fine-grained PAT with `Contents: read and write` on that repo).
  line 220-259: `git commit` + `git push` with those persisted credentials.

So anyone able to land a workflow file on a branch named `name: Agent Review Panel` can drive a job that pushes to a second repository using a PAT this repository's read-only `permissions:` block otherwise deliberately withholds. It also lets a forged run repeatedly occupy the `capture-collect` concurrency group (line 109-111, `cancel-in-progress: false`), queueing out real collections. The docs added in this change (docs/design/harness-engineering.md, docs/tasks/active/20260825-…-todo.md item 1) acknowledge the gap and defer it to a maintainer, so this is a known-and-recorded exposure rather than an oversight — but the guard is still absent and the new test that would have pinned it is written to take a (file, job) pair and simply does not list this file.

verdict.reason: Verified independently; no counterexample exists. capture-collect.yml consumes workflow_run by display name (lines 67-69) with no branches: filter, and its only job condition (line 129) gates solely on conclusion != 'skipped' — no path, no head_branch, no head_repository.full_name == github.repository, and no environment: key, so the secret is not behind an approval gate either. A repo-wide grep for workflow_run.path / head_repository / head_branch matches docker-publish.yml:70-71, publish-ghpage.yml:45-46, agent-review-panel.yml:166-167, agent-iterate-ci.yml:54-56 and ci-report.yml:56 but NONE in capture-collect.yml, so the guard does not exist under another name, in a helper, or via an include. The new test at scripts/agent/checks.test.mjs:580-584 enumerates exactly the three CI consumers and additionally requires workflows [CI] at :588, which this file does not have, so it structurally cannot cover it; the existing pins on this workflow (collect-captures.test.mjs:1048-1107, :1248-1273, :1316-1330) cover the permissions block, absence of ref:, and the skipped-conclusion string by exact equality — none pin trigger provenance. The job holds a cross-repo write PAT (secrets.EVAL_STORE_TOKEN, lines 142-146) with credentials persisted, pushes with it (lines 220-259), and sits in a non-cancellable concurrency group (lines 109-111), so a run of any workflow merely named "Agent Review Panel" — including a fork-PR run, the exact case the sibling workflows' head_repository checks exist for — drives it. In-lane missing authorization gate on a privileged workflow; blocking at major. Bounding note rather than a refutation: collect-captures.test.mjs:1248-1273 pins that no ref: and no head_* value selects code, so a forged trigger executes only default-branch code and cannot exfiltrate the PAT via code execution; the residual exposure is unauthorized invocation of the PAT-holding push job plus indefinite queue occupancy, not full token compromise.

searchedFor: Grep 'create-github-app-token' with 8 lines of context across .github/workflows
Compared against agent-fix.yml:121-129 and agent-review-panel.yml:1488-1493 / 1800-1808 (pinned + permission-scoped)
finding.summary: The fixer arm this change hardens still mints a full-installation App token from a mutable `@v1` tag and hands it to a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code
finding.evidence:
agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-115:

  - name: Generate GitHub App token
    id: app-token
    uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v1        # mutable tag, handles AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY
    with:
      app-id: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_ID }}
      private-key: ${{ secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
                                                    # <- no permission-* inputs at all
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
      token: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}

Two defects in one step. (a) Unpinned: every other consumer in this repo pins `@d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 # v1.12.0` and says why (agent-review-panel.yml:1485-1488 "Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key"). A compromised or retagged `v1` sees `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, i.e. the whole installation, not one token. (b) Unscoped: with no `permission-*` inputs the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — compare agent-fix.yml:121-129 and agent-review-panel.yml:1800-1808, which scope theirs precisely because "this token is live in a job that later checks out and executes untrusted branch code", which is exactly what happens on the next line here (the fixer agent installs, builds and tests the PR branch).

This is directly coupled to the change under review: the diff's justification for the new `path` clause is that a forged `name: CI` run "would otherwise drive this workflow's `contents: write` fixer". Closing the trigger while the token stays full-installation and mutable-tagged leaves the larger half of that arm's blast radius intact. Same pattern at agent-implement.yml:119 and agent-review-reply.yml:126. Recorded as maintainer work in docs/tasks/active/20260825-…-todo.md item 2, but still present in the tree.

verdict.reason: The quoted code is present exactly as described. agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 mints an App installation token via actions/create-github-app-token@v1 (mutable tag, handling AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) with no permission-* inputs, so the token carries the installation's full permission set. That token is handed to actions/checkout@v4 at :111-115 for the untrusted ref github.event.workflow_run.head_branch with no persist-credentials: false, and the same job then executes branch-controlled code (pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at :285) and exposes the token as GH_TOKEN at :463 and :523. The repo's own convention contradicts this: agent-fix.yml:119-130 pins the SHA d72941d797fd3113feb6b93fd0dec494b13a2547 (v1.12.0) and scopes permission-contents/pull-requests/issues, with a comment stating the reason is precisely that the token is live in a job that later checks out and executes untrusted branch code. Ten of thirteen call sites pin; only agent-iterate-ci.yml:106, agent-implement.yml:119 and agent-review-reply.yml:126 do not. The trusted-script staging at :136-146 self-documents that it only removes the branch-code-with-a-write-token half and does not narrow the token. docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:190-208 acknowledges the issue as outstanding and that the new trigger filter only narrows the forgery surface. No refutation ground applies: the managed gate at :91 controls who can trigger the job, not token scope or action mutability. In-lane (secret handling, least privilege, supply-chain integrity of a credential-handling action); major impact.

searchedFor: compared pinning/scoping between agent-implement.yml, agent-iterate-ci.yml and the panel/rerun/loop/ci-report uses
finding.summary: The author/fixer paths mint an UNSCOPED GitHub App installation token from a mutable action tag, which is what makes the gate-2 forgery above reachable
finding.evidence: agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 call `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` with `app-id`/`private-key` and NO `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token carries every permission the installation holds — handed to a job that then executes model-directed code with the branch checked out. Every other consumer in this repo scopes the token explicitly and pins the action to an immutable SHA for exactly this reason: agent-review-panel.yml:1483-1493 ("Pinned to an immutable commit SHA (not the movable @v1 tag) for supply-chain safety — this action handles the App private key", plus `permission-pull-requests: write` / `permission-issues: write`), agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87, ci-report.yml:86-94. Two consequences: (1) if the installation carries `Checks: write`, the unscoped token lets the author agent post its own `agent-review-*` check runs, which `checkPassed` accepts because it never checks `app.slug` — that is the gate-2 bypass reported separately; (2) a compromised or retagged `@v1` reads `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`. Pre-existing and outside the diff, but the diff's whole premise is that these gates are unforgeable, and the token scope is what decides that.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim verifies against the tree. agent-implement.yml:117-122 and agent-iterate-ci.yml:104-109 both mint an App installation token via the mutable `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` tag with only app-id/private-key and NO `permission-*` inputs, so the token inherits the installation's full permission set. That token is then handed to model-directed execution with the branch checked out: agent-implement.yml:200 (checkout token) and 353-357 (github_token to claude-code-action), plus agent-iterate-ci.yml:115 and 372-375 (fixer agent over attacker-influenceable branch code). The claimed in-repo contrast is real and even stronger than stated: agent-review-panel.yml:1797-1810 pins an immutable SHA and scopes contents/pull-requests/issues with the explicit comment 'Least privilege ... this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code' - the exact invariant the two flagged jobs omit; agent-review-panel.yml:1485-1493, agent-rerun.yml:94-98, agent-loop.yml:83-87 and ci-report.yml:86-94 all pin and scope likewise. No guard neutralizes it: the actor write-access check (agent-implement.yml:101-113) and the managed-branch gate (agent-iterate-ci.yml:91) constrain who can trigger the run, not the credential's blast radius inside the agent step. In lane (secrets / least-privilege credential exposure, plus a mutable-tag action reading AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY), major impact. I cannot enumerate the installation's granted permissions from the repo, so full exploitability (e.g. checks:write enabling self-posted agent-review-* check runs) stays unproven - that uncertainty keeps the finding rather than refuting it.
